taskVersion.name: pilot-ves-label-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Choba-LawnTennisField, Lawn Tennis Field, University of Port Harcourt, Choba Town. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 91.2 | 2.535 | 2.535
2 | 380.2 | 15.83 | 18.37
3 | 43.25 | 20.36 | 38.73
4 | 474.3 | 33.05 | 71.78
5 | 597.1 | - | -

What is the curve type of this station? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve-type notation for the given VES station, we analyze the resistivities of the layers in depth order:

1.  **Layer Resistivities:**
    *   $r_1 = 91.2$ $\Omega\text{m}$
    *   $r_2 = 380.2$ $\Omega\text{m}$
    *   $r_3 = 43.25$ $\Omega\text{m}$
    *   $r_4 = 474.3$ $\Omega\text{m}$
    *   $r_5 = 597.1$ $\Omega\text{m}$

2.  **Analyze Consecutive Groups of Three Layers:**
    *   **Group 1 (Layers 1-2-3):** $r_1=91.2$, $r_2=380.2$, $r_3=43.25$.
        Since $r_1 < r_2$ and $r_2 > r_3$ ($91.2 < 380.2 > 43.25$), the pattern is **K**.
    *   **Group 2 (Layers 2-3-4):** $r_2=380.2$, $r_3=43.25$, $r_4=474.3$.
        Since $r_2 > r_3$ and $r_3 < r_4$ ($380.2 > 43.25 < 474.3$), the pattern is **H**.
    *   **Group 3 (Layers 3-4-5):** $r_3=43.25$, $r_4=474.3$, $r_5=597.1$.
        Since $r_3 < r_4$ and $r_4 < r_5$ ($43.25 < 474.3 < 597.1$), the pattern is **A**.

3.  **Combine the Letters:**
    The sequence of letters for the 5 layers is **KHA**.

{"curve_type": "KHA"}
